newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-THUMBS UP FOR WEBSTER IN EURO GRAND PRIX.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-THUMBS UP FOR WEBSTER IN EURO GRAND PRIX.

text.p: Englishman Steve Webster played through pain to be only one stroke off the course record when setting the pace in the European Grand Prix opening round at Slaley Hall on Thursday.

Webster trapped his thumb in his car door after returning home from missing the cut in the Tournament Players Championship in Hamburg on Friday, but decided to play and was rewarded with a six-under-par 66.
This was two strokes better than Sweden's Mats Hallberg, Juan Carlos Pinero of Spain, who bogeyed the last two holes, and another Englishman, Steven Bottomley.
Reigning European number one Colin Montgomerie was one of only two players not to drop a shot during the morning rounds as a three-birdie 69 took him within three shots of the lead.
Defending champion Retief Goosen of South Africa was the other player with a clean card for a 69, too, his shots picked up with an eagle and birdie.
Webster, the 1995 European Tour qualifying school winner, who then lost his card and had to requalify last year, fashioned his lead with an eagle and six birdies, also running up two bogeys.
"The thumb was so painful I didn't think I'd be able to play," said Webster. "I couldn't hit a ball for four days and played only nine holes practice before deciding to try to get round.
"I couldn't leave the thumb bandaged because it wouldn't fit over a glove, so I made do with a plaster and it made the thumb very sore, so I only hit four drivers all day."
